lead: a family sells the house, takes the job, gives the notice — none of that is yours. yours is the morning it all has to move, both ends of that day, and a hallway four hundred miles off.
sun: the decision was made months back by people who then had to get through it, and getting through it is the part you own: the emptying, the road, the kettle found before you go. what they keep afterwards is having moved. from inside the van it is a route with a stop on it, and the stop is a hallway where the last box goes down and you are thanked at a door.
moon: The Gate has you at that house before anybody is dressed — first vehicle on the street, straps out at six — and the same speed puts you in the new town ahead of them, so the first face there is yours. what it cannot supply is the second week. whatever in you moves quickest is spent on one morning, and the mornings all belong to somebody else's arrival.
pull: you are the last of the old town and the first of the new one, and both of those jobs are one day long.
tension: what a customer keeps of the move is its final hour — how quickly the van emptied, that the beds were up by dark. the four hundred miles belong to nobody, since they slept through part of it and you were alone for the rest. so every recommendation praises how quick you were, quick being the smallest true thing about it, and a household that has moved once has no reason to call you again.
cost: nine hundred hallways have had a last box set down in them by you. a household gets out of one town at six in the morning and eats in another by nine at night without anybody in it thinking about how, which happens because one person holds both ends and hands nothing over in the middle. each of those addresses is a house you have never sat down in.

lead: three of them got out of that house and you drove all three. the youngest tells it as a decision she made at twenty, and what she had to be walked past has been in you since you were fifteen.
sun: each was already going — your brother had the offer, your sister had the night she could not stay through, your mother had the letter about the flat. what none of them had was the way. so it was you packing at two in the morning, four changes of train, a week on a floor in a city you do not live in, then a platform, alone, with the far side behind you.
moon: The Bearer keeps the reason. what that house was like in the years before your brother and sister were old enough to look at it went in at fifteen and has not come out — no evening, no funeral, nobody with a use for it. a term this long has no delivery date, since handing it over would happen at a door, and the door is where you turn round.
pull: the leaving worked, three times over. what they were leaving is still in you, full term, at the size it went in, handed to nobody.
tension: the version that holds at family gatherings is that you were the one who stayed, said kindly, with a small allowance made for you, since staying is what people do when they cannot manage a leaving. your sister has said it twice in front of her children. correcting it means telling three adults in their forties what their childhood actually was and who moved them out of it, and that does not fit into an afternoon in a garden.
cost: nobody had to say out loud what they were leaving. that is why all three went, and went quietly, in one night each, with a bag and a train time. each of them arrived somewhere holding a clean account of how they got there. the version with the reasons in it sits in the one person nobody has thought to ask.

lead: she had four thousand pounds she did not know was hers, and she believes an office found it. she had written twice and given up. the finding took nine months and happened in buildings she would not go into alone.
sun: people turn up already owed and already trying — the pension unclaimed eleven years, the estate stuck on one signature, the payment refused twice on a technicality. the wanting is not your doing. the route is: which floor, which form, which sentence changes the tone, the chair beside them at the hearing. it lands in an account with your name nowhere on it, and the day it lands is the day you stop.
moon: several of you handle money and they have never been introduced. one will give nine months to a stranger's four thousand. one has not opened a brown envelope since spring. one lent a cousin more than could be spared and never raised it. each is competent in its own range and unreachable from the rest, so no figure exists for what you have got people, or for what you have.
pull: you know the way to money for anybody who is owed it. the several of you who walk that road have never been in a room together about your own.
tension: the ones you get there tell it two ways, both wrong the same way. some thank an institution, since nine months of appointments must have come from somewhere official. the rest tell it as a favour done one afternoon. neither version has room for six people in one body taking a stretch each — one of you at the start, another on the appeal — and saying so the week a cheque clears sounds like asking to be thanked.
cost: nobody else makes the fourteenth phone call, and the fourteenth is usually the one, which is why money that sat for a decade is now in the accounts of people who had stopped believing in it. nobody in you has been assigned to your own paperwork. and you have never seen what any of it did — what the four thousand bought, how the eleven years got spoken of after.

lead: thirty years of eating at other people's rate — their hour, their portion, their idea of enough. what happens on the way back from those tables, alone, has never been seen by any of them.
sun: you go in front on the route — which door, which stairs, how long a day can be made to last — and the body does the whole of it at their speed: their four cigarettes, their sandwich at whatever hour they manage one. months of that, and it ends the way they all end, on a pavement, with them going in and you turning for the car on an appetite held since breakfast.
moon: The Follower declined the front a long time ago and has not reconsidered. so you are second to the plate at every table, slightly behind whoever is being taken, a little less than them on purpose, and it passes for good manners. the standard being matched is a different person each time. a lifetime of matching other people's appetites made one body, and that body kept every bit of it.
pull: there is no rate of your own — only whoever you are walking beside, matched the whole way. the far side is a garage counter at midnight with nobody left to keep pace with.
tension: you get described as a man who barely eats, by people who have eaten beside you for years and are not inventing it. the figures at a health check disagree with their account, and the face a doctor makes reading them is a thing you have now watched four times. explaining it means describing the drive home to somebody who was only ever in the car on the way out, and the way out is the half they were fed.
cost: a man ashamed of how he eats can sit down across from you and never feel measured, because you are behind him and you stay behind him, and that is why some of them ate at all. what accumulates does it on the return leg, quietly, over three decades, and it is on you now in an amount that no meal anyone has watched you eat could account for.
